task_text: IKEA MuJoCo KYRRE stool (IKEA KYRRE stool (AA-2118871-4), manual step 1: three legs, six screws) with two 7-DoF Franka Panda arms, each with the MuJoCo Menagerie Panda hand (two-finger, tendon-coupled). Fasten the three legs to the upside-down seat of the KYRRE stool: place each leg and drive its two screws, in the scene's order (leg 1, its two screws, leg 2, its two screws, leg 3, its two screws), and leave the stool upside-down on the table. Success requirements: All nine retention welds (three legs, six screws) are engaged, each by its operation's acceptance gates, strictly in the scene's operation order. Every operation is still within its gates: worst connector gap below 0.6 mm (a screw's seat gap 0.7 mm), lateral within 0.8 mm, axis within 2 degrees; every screw head is seated on its leg's bearing pad. The assembly stayed rigid after the last weld: every part within 1 mm and 1 degree of its pose relative to the seat at that moment. At the end it is released (no robot contact with any part), and all of the above held for 1.5 s with the seat drifting less than 1 cm and tilting less than 3 degrees over the hold. The benchmark's terminal rules, the same in every IKEA MuJoCo task, come on top of these requirements. When your rows end: (1) the requirements above hold; (2) the parts are released: no robot link touches any part; (3) every part is at rest: at most 0.01 m/s and 0.05 rad/s; (4) the simulation never broke down: no non-finite state, no MuJoCo BADQACC / BADQPOS / BADQVEL warning, no contact of a part deeper than 10 mm, at any time. The grader then holds your last row for 1.0 s more and requires (1)-(4) again at its end. Mechanism: One retention weld per operation, switched on with the current relative pose once its gates hold for 0.15 s: the previous operation latched, gap, lateral and tilt near the seat, at least 4 mm of travel, contact with the counterpart, slow, and for a screw more than a quarter turn of tightening. The screw threads (0.5 mm pitch, right-hand) are contact geometry: a screw advances only by being turned. Once a part's weld latches, it stops colliding with the seat and with the other parts welded to it (it still collides with the robot, the table and every unwelded part), and a latched screw and its insert's thread stop colliding altogether (sw_cutover.json: from the first operation on). Each leg still carries the idle spring jaw of its removed press-in pin.
